title: Sim fog uses a lagging entity region, so enemy positions inside hidden regions reach Belief frames, belief and features
description: Observe() decides whether an enemy is visible with `visible.Contains(e.Region)`. It then reports `e.Position`, the live exact cell. AdvanceMovement (line 485) only updates `e.Region` when the unit reaches the next region's center. While an enemy walks from a visible region into a hidden one, the observer keeps getting its exact position until the unit is at the hidden region's center. That includes where it went. BeliefModel records the contact with `LastSeenRegion = RegionOf(position)`, which is the hidden region, at confidence 1. FeatureCompiler then marks that never-seen region as Enemy or Contested. It can also raise EnemyExpansionSeen, and threats are computed from it. All of this goes into StrategistContext and the Claude prompt.
failure_scenario: I ran a scratch test (since deleted): MatchHarness with the selector against rush on TwinValley, 600 s, seeds 1, 2 and 3. In 262 of 9000 frames per match the arm's Belief frame had an enemy whose RegionOf(position) was not in VisibleRegions. Example: t=393.6 s, enemy HARV id 11 at (65,63) in region 6 (lane-south-east), 15.6 cells from its center, with visible regions {0,1,4}. For seed 1, in 1401 frames BeliefSnapshot.Enemies held a contact in a region the arm had never seen at any point. In 1118 frames MapControl.Control marked such a never-seen region Enemy or Contested.
suggested_fix: Test enemy visibility against the region the unit is actually in, `map.Map.RegionOf(e.Position)` (the same rule IsEventForPlayer uses for events). Or update `e.Region` on every movement step from the position. Add a regression test for this invariant: every non-own entity in a Belief frame must have RegionOf(Position) in VisibleRegions, checked over a full match.

title: Leakage probe cannot detect the transit leak, and the arena reports 0 leakage while features leak
description: PerturbHidden only changes enemy credits and queues, which have no field in ObservationFrame, and spawns one silent, stationary unit exactly at a hidden region's center. No enemy is moving, no event is emitted and no entity sits near a region boundary. So the probe never exercises the paths that actually leak: the position/region mismatch in Observe, and event delivery. LeakageProbe.Run then compares only 15 frames (compareSeconds = 1) on one map and one seed. FogAndFreshnessTests and SkirmishSimulationFogTests use the same perturbation. The arena report's 'Differing frames 0/N' and the passing unit tests therefore claim the fog invariant holds when it does not.
failure_scenario: On the same build, FogAndFreshnessTests.Perturbing_hidden_simulator_state_leaves_the_strategist_context_hash_unchanged passes. The arena probe also reports 0 differing frames. Yet the Belief-mode strategist context in the same kind of match contains contacts and Enemy control in regions the arm never saw, in 1118 of 9000 frames.
suggested_fix: Also perturb moving hidden state, for example redirect a hidden enemy unit's path, or teleport an enemy that is visible only because of a region lag. Emit the perturbation's events through the normal path rather than silently. Compare over a longer window, or compare Belief frames directly, with a per-frame invariant check: every non-own entity and every non-own event position must be in VisibleRegions. Run it on several maps and seeds.

title: The arena logs Claude failures a second time with stopwatch latency; the extra record makes hashes nondeterministic and cannot be replayed
description: BotAgentFactory subscribes to ClaudeStrategist.ProposalFailed and writes failure.ToDecisionRecord(...) into the arm's decision log. That record has kind strategy.proposal_failed with a different schema ({strategist, code, detail, cost, rawResponse}, no role or reason), and its cost.latencySeconds comes from the ClaudeStrategist Stopwatch (ClaudeStrategist.cs:210,293). SimulatedLatencyStrategist replaces LatencySeconds only on successful proposals, so the fixed --llm-latency does not cover failures. The scheduler then logs its own no_opinion proposal_failed for the same request. ReplayStrategist skips the extra record (no role), and a replay never emits it.
failure_scenario: Not triggered in practice: across all opponents and all maps for llm, llm+fast and llm-shadow (seeds 1 and 2) the fake client produced zero Claude failures. The failure scenario is from reading the code. Take any Claude failure in an llm arm, such as MappingFailed, ParseFailed, RefinePlaybookSwitch, or a live timeout or rate limit. The log gains a record like {"kind":"strategy.proposal_failed",...{"strategist":"claude-strategic","code":"mapping_failed","cost":{"latencySeconds":0.00213...}}}. First, running the same match twice gives different decisionLogHash values even with a fixed simulated latency. Second, replaying the log with ReplayStrategist can never reproduce that record, so the replayed hash always differs.
suggested_fix: Write Claude failure details under a separate record kind that is kept out of the hashed decision log, or strip or replace latencySeconds with the game-time latency before logging. Have ReplayStrategist re-emit the record from the recording, or exclude that kind from the replay hash. At a minimum, give the record a kind other than strategy.proposal_failed so it cannot be confused with scheduler failure records.

title: Bandit arm learns from held-out matches, so its held-out win rate is not a held-out result
description: The shared ContextualBanditStrategist gets CompleteEpisode(Reward(...)) in onFinish for every job, whatever its split. Program.Jobs orders jobs opponent → map (training, then heldout) → seed, and the bandit runs them one after another. With `--maps all` (or `heldout`), the result of each held-out match updates the policy that plays the next held-out seed on the same map, and the next opponent's matches. The report still labels these rows `heldout`. This breaks the spec's rule that held-out maps are never used for tuning.
failure_scenario: `arena run --arms bandit --maps all --opponents rush,turtle --seeds 4`: the bandit plays open-steppe seed 1 vs rush, is rewarded, and then plays open-steppe seeds 2 to 4 and every turtle held-out match with a policy fitted to held-out outcomes. The `bandit | heldout` win-rate row is reported as generalisation, but it is in-sample.
suggested_fix: Only call CompleteEpisode for training-split jobs (pass the split into the factory or agent). Freeze the bandit, or run it on a snapshot of its policy, for held-out jobs. Order the jobs so that all training matches finish before any held-out match.

title: Seeds are not independent samples, and odd seed counts (default 1) bias the arm's faction
description: The only simulator randomness is rally-point jitter, and the bots are deterministic, so a match outcome is set almost entirely by seed parity (the faction assignment). The report counts every seed as one match, which overstates the sample size. The CLI default is `--seeds 1`, so the arm is always Allied. Any odd seed count gives it one more Allied game than Soviet game. The report nevertheless claims the faction asymmetry 'does not bias an arm's results'.
failure_scenario: In 60 scratch mirror matches (balanced, rush and tech on all 5 maps, seeds 1-4), seeds 1 and 3 and seeds 2 and 4 had the same winner in 28 of 30 pairs. In tech-vs-tech, seeds 1 and 3 ended with identical asset values on every map (e.g. fortress-choke 20300 v 1800 for both). Allied won every balanced mirror on 3 of 5 maps. A default run (`--seeds 1`) reports a win rate that is really the Allied-vs-Soviet matchup, as '1/1 matches'.
suggested_fix: Make seeds affect play: add seeded noise in the bot's timing and targeting, or combat variance in the sim. Require an even seed count, or run both faction assignments per seed. Report effective distinct outcomes, or per-faction counts, next to the win rate.

title: Timeout winner and trade efficiency use an asset value that leaves out prepaid production and values a ConYard at 0
description: AssetValue = credits + fixture cost of live entities. ApplyProduce takes the full cost up front, but queued, in-progress and awaiting-placement items are not counted, so a player who is producing at the time limit loses that value. The fixture prices GAYARD and NACNST at 0, so deploying the MCV drops asset value by 3000. A player who never deploys keeps +3000. MatchRunner's trade efficiency credits 0 for destroying a construction yard. Timeouts are frequent: 14 of the 60 mirror matches ended by timeout.
failure_scenario: Scratch run on fortress-choke with MaxSeconds 60. Both players deploy; P0 queues GAPOWR, which completes and waits for placement. At timeout P0 = 9200 and P1 = 10000, so P1 wins with less material. In a second run where only P0 deploys: P0 = 10000, P1 = 13000, so the idle, undeployed MCV wins the timeout.
suggested_fix: Include the cost of queue items, pending placements and in-progress production in AssetValue. Give construction yards the MCV's value (3000) in the fixture, or map a deployed yard back to its MCV cost for valuation and destroyed-value accounting.

title: Inference cost leaves out billed tokens from failed LLM requests (refusal, max_tokens, parse or mapping failure)
description: ClaudeStrategist.Fail passes the real token cost for refusal, max-tokens, unexpected-stop, parse-failed, mapping-failed and refine-switch failures (ClaudeStrategist.cs:228-253). The arena logs these as ProposalFailed records that include `cost`. BotArenaAgent.Finish adds up tokens and USD only for Proposal and ShadowProposal records, so the tokens spent on failed requests never reach the report. The code comment at line 97 ('Failed requests still cost tokens') acknowledges this but does nothing about it. An arm whose model often returns malformed JSON therefore looks cheaper per match.
failure_scenario: The llm arm, with a model that returns unparseable JSON on half its calls: each failure bills its input and output tokens (ProposalFailed.cost.inputTokens > 0), but Stats.TokensIn and Stats.Usd count only the successful half, so the reported $/match is about half the real cost.
suggested_fix: Include DecisionRecordKinds.ProposalFailed records that have a `cost` object in the token and USD sums (and in the llm+fast refine calls). Report failed-request cost as its own column.

title: Invalid-plan and lateness metrics mix deterministic fallback proposals into the LLM arm's figures
description: Proposals, Rejected and LateSeconds include Fallback-role proposals from the selector fallback, which have zero latency and are always valid. When the LLM fails, the fallback runs more often, which lowers mean lateness and the invalid-plan rate. A worse LLM therefore scores better on both metrics, and the arm's figures do not describe the strategist being evaluated.
failure_scenario: Scratch llm --llm-fake match (twin-valley, seed 2): Primary n=68, mean lateness 4.00 s; Fallback n=5, 0.00 s. The report shows 3.73 s over 73 proposals. With more LLM failures the gap grows.
suggested_fix: Group proposal, rejection and lateness figures by role (Primary, Fallback, Emergency), using the `role` field already in the Proposal and Validation records. Report the primary strategist's figures as the arm metric.

title: Production speed uses every Production building for every queue and keeps going after the right factory is lost
description: CountFactories counts every Role==Production building (ConYard, barracks, war factory), and multiplier = sqrt(count) applies to every queue. In RA2 a queue's speed depends on the number of factories of its own kind, and a queue stops when its last factory is destroyed. Here a barracks speeds up tank and building production. An in-progress vehicle queue keeps building, and spawns at the last building (any type), after the war factory is destroyed.
failure_scenario: An Allied base with GAYARD, GAPILE and GAWEAP builds GAPOWR (48 s) in 48/√3 ≈ 27.7 s. An enemy raid that destroys GAWEAP does not stop the queued MTNKs: they finish at √2 speed and appear next to a power plant. Harass and snipe playbooks, which are meant to punish losing production, are under-rewarded.
suggested_fix: Map each QueueKind to its factory type (Building → yard, Infantry → barracks, Vehicle → war factory, Aircraft → airfield). Count only those factories for that queue's multiplier, pause the queue when the count is 0, and spawn units at a factory of that type.

title: Sim accepts AttackCommand on fogged or never-seen enemies and routes units to the target's true hidden region
description: ApplyAttack looks up the target with `entities.Find(e => e.Id == c.Target && e.Alive)` and never checks whether the attacker's owner can see it. It then paths the attackers to `target.Region`, which is the engine's current, hidden location, and sets FinalDestination to that region's centre. SquadController.Tick sends AttackCommand for any contact up to MaxContactAgeSeconds (20 s) old, including contacts that are no longer visible, so a Belief-mode bot follows enemies through fog to their real positions. The same path also accepts attacks on ids the player has never seen (entity ids are sequential and easy to guess), and the unit walks across the map to the enemy's real location. This is engine-omniscient state driving play in Belief mode. The leakage probe cannot see it, because it only hashes StrategistContext for 1 s and never looks at command outcomes or unit movement.
failure_scenario: Demonstrated with a temporary xunit test on TestMaps.TwoPlayerCombat (since deleted). (1) Stale contact: an enemy MCV is seen at X=20 (battlefield), our watcher leaves, and the enemy moves in fog to X=30 (start-b). The belief frame no longer contains it and only region 0 is visible. We send AttackCommand(tank, enemyId), as SquadController does for a contact under 20 s old. After 40 s the tank is at X=30 and the enemy is dead, with rejected=0. The tank should have gone to the last-seen X=20 or had the order rejected. (2) Never-seen id: our belief frame contains only ids 1 and 3. AttackCommand on guessed id 2 (the enemy's hidden MCV) is accepted (rejected=0). The tank walks three regions to X=30 and kills the MCV, which leaves p1 with 0 entities and wins the match from a pure id guess.
suggested_fix: In ApplyAttack, reject the command (RejectedCommands++) unless the target is in a region currently visible to `player` (VisibleRegionsFor(player).Contains(target.Region)). Also drop an explicit target, and stop re-pathing toward it, once it leaves the owner's vision; do not route to the hidden target.Region. Add a fog test that attacks a fogged or never-seen id and asserts rejection and no movement toward the hidden region. Consider extending the arena leakage probe to compare submitted commands, or own-unit positions, over a longer window.

title: Harvesters still earn credits after their refinery is sold or destroyed
description: The refinery region is chosen once, when harvesting ends (TargetRefineryRegion). The ToRefinery and Unloading phases never check that a refinery still exists there, so Unloading adds CarriedValue to credits after the refinery is gone. This removes the main economic payoff of raiding a refinery in RA2, and it gives a player who has lost or sold its refinery 700 credits per harvester already on its way back. failure_scenario: Demonstrated with a temporary test on TestMaps.TwoPlayerCombat. Deploy the MCV, build test-refinery, add a harvester, step until Phase == ToRefinery, then sell the refinery. In the arena, a harass or rush that kills a refinery does not stop the income already in transit, which makes raid playbooks look weaker.
suggested_fix: In ToRefinery and Unloading, check that a living Economy building owned by the player is still in TargetRefineryRegion. If there is none, send the harvester to NearestRefineryRegion again, or keep it waiting with its load. Do not harvest when the player has no refinery at all.

title: Power has no effect on defenses: Tesla coils, Prism towers and Patriots keep firing during low power
description: ComputePower is used only by AdvanceProduction, which halves the build rate on low power. ResolveCombat never consults power, so the fixture's powered defenses (NATSLA -75, GAPRIS -75, GAPATR -50, NAFLAK -50) fire at full damage with power far below demand. title: Refineries come without a free harvester, so the first income costs 3400 instead of RA2's 2000
description: ApplyPlace spawns only the building. In RA2 a refinery comes with a free harvester (FreeUnit=HARV/CMIN), and the rules contract has no field for it. With the fixture's prices (refinery 2000, HARV and CMIN 1400, 10000 starting credits, and no starting harvester) every expansion refinery earns nothing until a 1400 harvester is also built. That depends on the war factory, which is serialized behind other items. The economy tempo, the value of expanding and the Expand and economy playbooks are all mis-scaled compared with RA2, and a refinery built with no harvester queued is 2000 credits of dead value that still counts toward the timeout asset score.

In the sim they stay flat until it has built GAWEAP (2000) and a HARV (1400, 84 s build). The opening income curve is minutes late, and results that depend on economic timing (rush against eco, expansion value) cannot be carried over to RA2.
